title: Electromagnetism and Induction
seo_title: Electromagnetism Worksheets: Electromagnets, Induction, Motors and Generators (Physics)
standard_text: Plan and conduct an investigation to provide evidence that an electric current can produce a magnetic field and that a changing magnetic field can produce an electric current.
meta_desc: Free high school physics worksheets on electromagnetism (NGSS HS-PS2-5): magnetic fields from currents, electromagnets, electromagnetic induction, motors, generators and transformers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Currents make fields; changing fields make currents.
key_sub: Electromagnets, motors, generators and transformers all use this link.
body_html:
How to think about it

Electricity and magnetism are two sides of one force.

  • A current makes a magnetic field. A coil with an iron core is an electromagnet; more turns or more current make it stronger.
  • A changing magnetic field through a coil induces a current. Faster change, stronger magnet or more turns → more current.
  • Motors: current → motion. Generators: motion → current. Transformers: changing current → current in a second coil.
Example

Magnet held still in a coil. Current?

The field is not changing

Answer: none

Example

Double the turns on an electromagnet?

More turns → stronger field

Answer: stronger

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a still magnet in a coil makes a current.
  • Thinking a generator creates energy from nothing.
  • Mixing up motors and generators.

faq.q: How does an electric current make a magnetic field?
faq.a: Moving charges in a wire create a magnetic field around it. Winding the wire into a coil concentrates the field.
When the magnetic field through a coil changes, a current is induced in the coil. A faster change gives a larger current.

faq.q: What is the difference between a motor and a generator?
faq.a: A motor uses current in a magnetic field to make motion. A generator uses motion in a magnetic field to make current.
